markers.interpretation: DNA can provide limited risk context for some skin traits, but it cannot identify a makeup, skincare, or fragrance allergen or predict an individual product reaction. Acne caused by pore-clogging products (acne cosmetica), allergic contact dermatitis, irritation, and rosacea flares are different problems; assess symptoms and exposures. Alcohol-related flushing after drinking is separate from irritation after a topical product. Patch testing by a clinician can help identify allergic contact dermatitis.
do_not_claim: a specific cosmetic or skincare allergy
topical alcohol sensitivity or alcohol-caused acne
product-triggered rosacea or acne from genotype
confirm_with: sun exposure and product exposure history
clinician-directed patch testing when contact allergy is suspected
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Consumer DNA cannot identify the ingredient causing an individual rash, irritation, acne cosmetica, or rosacea flare. Product history and symptoms matter; suspected allergic contact dermatitis may need clinician-directed patch testing.
